title: Review of c28's ringswim SIBMD (C:swim-divide) on fresh seed 7: replicated; ring >= 1.5 in 99.9% of cell-frames, 47 ringed swimmers >= 3 BL, 102 persistent splits (400 t rule), and two lineages that swim ringed and then divide into ringed daughters (#599 6.6 BL; #613 -> #707 swims 4.4 BL)
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on seed 7: a labkit pack (256^2, t=10000) and the claim's ringtrack.py to t=20000, plus a snapshot re-run to t=17800 for one division (img/div_s7_613.png, the claim's divview.py). labkit: from smoothed noise, 34-40 cells, L membrane-like (rim/core 1.59, rim/out 5.1, 160/214 individuals), 72 long-lived tracks move >= 1 body length, max 4.2. ringtrack: 31626 cell-frames with median contour ring 2.05, 99.9% >= 1.5; 102 persistent splits (both children survive 400 t without re-merging); 47 tracks swim >= 3 body lengths, all ringed; lineage_report finds #599 (6.58 BL, ring 2.01, divides into #794/#796) and #613 (3.18 BL, divides at t~17260 into #707 and #708, which keep the ring; #707 swims 4.38 BL). div_s7_613.png shows a clean binary pinch with a bright link rim on both daughters. The links are made inside the cells (b K S with K held in by phi^2 mobility), so the ring is self-made. As in the claim's own packs, labkit's stricter 1000 t window counts only 2 persistent splits (318 splits, 248 merges), so many divisions are undone by later fusions.

verdicts.track_note: seed 7 #613: ringed (median 2.01, 100% of frames) while it swims 3.18 BL, divides at t~17260 into #707 and #708, both ringed, #707 swims 4.38 BL (img/div_s7_613.png). I did not re-trace the claim's seed-1 #563.
verdicts.limitation: Division is in a fission-fusion regime: labkit's 1000 t window keeps only 2 persistent splits on my seed (claim packs 0-2), merge/split 0.78, so the 102 persistent splits rest on ringtrack's 400 t hold. Only 2 lineages per seed show all three together, and motion is modest (3-6.6 body lengths). The ring is placed by a drift up the wall indicator (written against phi), but the cells make the link themselves. One fresh seed; no dt or resolution test.
